summary: London Stansted Airport (STN) is the third-busiest airport serving London, located approximately 40 miles northeast of the city centre in Essex. Opened in its current form in 1991 with a terminal designed by architect Sir Norman Foster, the site originated as a WWII RAF base before becoming a major hub for low-cost European carriers, particularly Ryanair. It operates a single terminal and runway, handling around 28 million passengers annually.
faqs:
Q: Which airlines use London Stansted as a main hub?
A: Ryanair is by far the dominant carrier, operating the majority of flights. Other notable airlines include easyJet, Jet2, TUI, and Pegasus Airlines for select routes.

Q: How long does it take to travel from Stansted to central London?
A: The Stansted Express train reaches London Liverpool Street in roughly 45–50 minutes. By car or coach via the M11 motorway, the journey typically takes 60–90 minutes depending on traffic.

Q: Does Stansted Airport operate 24 hours?
A: No, Stansted has a strict night flight curfew. No scheduled flights operate between approximately 11:30 PM and 6:00 AM, though some delayed arrivals and emergency landings are permitted.

Q: When was the current Stansted terminal building completed?
A: The Norman Foster-designed terminal opened in March 1991, replacing the older wartime-era buildings on the same site.
transport_tips: The Stansted Express train is the fastest and most reliable option to central London, with departures every 15–30 minutes to Liverpool Street station.
